A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAT-STEER research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–C are readable and support a complete comparison; the additional page in v3 reflects layout reflow.

before.justification: v2 reports original QA and generation experiments, component ablations, token-selection analyses and additional transfer evaluations in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–9, performance plots and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same attribute-specific gates, MMD alignment, positive-preservation, sparsity and orthogonality penalties, activation normalization and overall training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use TruthfulQA, Toxigen, BBQ, HelpSteer, ParaDetox, FaithEval, HH-RLHF and OpenBookQA for the same tasks and scenarios. No dataset, attribute or evaluation domain is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including the ICL, SFT and LITO subsets evaluated on HH-RLHF and OpenBookQA. RAdapt's citation changes from Yang et al. (2024c) to (2024b), but still identifies the same MORAL work.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same model variants, data splits, sample counts, training settings and evaluation metrics. The appendix experiments also retain their original evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the component ablations, token-selection comparisons, data-efficiency and attribute-scaling studies, ParaDetox analysis, transfer and interference evaluations, and three FaithEval examples. Their questions and supporting evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: There are no changes to repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty-reporting practices or statistical testing. The same tables and plots are retained without additional statistical documentation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 and Figures 3–7 retain the same results. For example, Table 1 still reports MAT-STEER scores of 61.94, 57.59 and 60.32, and Figure 3 retains the 55.82% HelpSteer win rate against LITO. Appendix findings and examples also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), their definitions and mathematical reasoning are unchanged, including Appendix A's kernel formulation of MMD. No formal assumption, theorem, proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about targeted multi-attribute steering, performance relative to ITI and fine-tuning methods, data efficiency and generalization. Their scope and headline quantitative claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, interpretation of the OpenBookQA trade-off and other findings remain unchanged. Both versions retain the same limitations concerning complex or unsteerable attributes, data dependence, restricted evaluation coverage and residual LLM risks.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same preprocessing instructions, intervention layers, LoRA settings, batch sizes, hyperparameter searches, kernel bandwidth, hardware and prompts. The code-access link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Nguyen et al. (2025a), Risk-aware distributional intervention policies for language models, in the introduction and Nguyen et al. (2025b), LASer, in Section 6. It removes Rui Yang et al. (2024), Rewards-in-context. The surrounding research-positioning argument remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Several references to 'Appendix A/C' become 'Section A/C', and the version/date annotation is updated. The section organization and almost all prose remain unchanged; there is no extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Text and floats reflow, particularly in the appendices: Table 4 moves from PDF page 14 to 15, and FaithEval Example 3 moves from page 16 to 17. The figures, table structures and example contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 makes limited citation updates and presentation adjustments while preserving the method, empirical evidence, technical documentation and limitations. The appendix reflow changes placement without losing content. These edits do not establish a meaningful net improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
